title: Nestorian Stele of Xi'an
summary: In 781, during the Tang dynasty, a stone monument was erected recording Christianity in China, which a University of Birmingham record dates from 635. Its inscription includes Syriac script. Unearthed in Zhouzhi, Shaanxi, in 1623, it is now kept in the Forest of Steles in Xi'an.

as_recorded.value: 7th day of the 1st month of the 2nd year of the Jianzhong period (that is, 781)
erected in 781 C.E. to commemorate the first coming of Christianity to China in the year 635 C.E.

where.modern_name: Forest of Steles, Xi'an, Shaanxi, China (current location of the stele)
where.historical_name: Tang China; the capital Chang'an is the modern Xi'an. The stele now stands in the Forest of Steles.

importance.justification: The monument is a key surviving record of early Christianity in Tang China.

sources.title: 大秦景教流行中國碑 (Da Qin jing jiao liu xing Zhongguo bei)
sources.publisher: University of Washington Libraries, East Asia Library
sources.author: Emily Jantz

reviewer_note: The pin is where the stele is held now, because neither page says where in Tang Chang'an it was first set up. The Birmingham record is marked unpublished. Syriac content is from the UW page.
